newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks start recovery on weak jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks start recovery on weak jobs data.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.375 +0.105 Gold NY 318.25 Lon fix 317.30
*Shares start to recover from their morning lows on June's weak jobs data, trade quiet. Vol 123.82 million, value A$297.46 million, 861 stocks traded, 281 steady, 205 up, 375 down.
Australian shares came off their lows on the release of weak June jobs data, which may pave the way for another cut in interest rates, but trade was quiet.
At 12.05 p.m. (0205 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.4 points down at 2,682.7, but off its low of 2,665.7 points.
The September share price index futures contracts was 17 points lower at 2,704, which was also off its low of 2,686 and kept a 21.4 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market is still likely to end the day weaker with the offshore falls in the gold and copper prices pushing the broader market lower.

Australian employment rose by just 11,900 in June after a fall of 40,300 in May, but full-time employment fell 16,900 in June and the participation rate also fell, giving an unemployment rate of 8.5 percent from 8.8 percent in May.
"The market liked the jobs numbers," said John Bowie-Wilson at BNP Equities.
Bowie-Wilson said these figures would auger well for another rate cut. The Reserve Bank of Australia last cut interest rates on May 23 by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent.
"There is not a lot of volume out there and a 13 point fall doesn't mean much in this market," he said.
Brokers said the market is likely to close between 10 and 20 points down after the 120 point fall on Wall Street overnight.
The biggest faller among the blue-chips was soft drinks group Coca-Cola Amatil, which fell over six percent after a downgrade by investment bank Merrill Lynch.

Resource stocks were also badly hit. Newcrest was almost seven percent down on rumours that it faced a margin call from ANZ Securities on its February equity-gold swap arrangement over its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy.
Brokers said Newcrest faced a margin call following the sharp slump in the bullion price.
Banks moved from negative territory into the positive zone following further bond yield falls on the weak jobs data.

Australian 10-year bonds fell to their lowest level in 3-1/2 years as the market braced for a monetary policy easing. At 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), the 10-year T-bond yield fell 11 percentage points to 6.62 percent.

At the same time, the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7419/24, compared with Wednesday's close at $0.7435/40, falling about 1/4 cents to test its 18-month low as another rate cut seemed inevitable.
